summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a right-handed male with mixed Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma involving the central nervous system and eyes, was admitted for a scheduled cycle of high-dose methotrexate and rituximab. He had a history of a mild allergic reaction to rituximab, so he was pre-treated with dexamethasone, Benadryl, ranitidine, and acetaminophen, which prevented any infusion reaction. Methotrexate was administered with IV and oral bicarbonate to promote renal excretion and protect kidney function. Leucovorin was started 12 hours post-infusion. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, reaching 0.2 by discharge, allowing for safe discontinuation of rescue therapy. His hospital course was uncomplicated, with stable vital signs, no fever, and no neurological changes. He was discharged home on a prednisone taper, short-course leucovorin and bicarbonate, and bowel regimen, with instructions to follow up for lab monitoring and ophthalmologic evaluation.
